# derived from monero v0.18.5.1 source, not captured from a run
# THE RESTRICTED-RPC PROBE'S ANSWER, and a WHOLE JSON-RPC ENVELOPE rather than a result object --
# the only file in tests/fixtures/node/ that is. fmonero-mock serves it verbatim except for `id`,
# which it overwrites with the id the request carried.
# WHERE IT COMES FROM: with --restricted-rpc (or --public-node) a gated json_rpc method is NOT
# REGISTERED AT ALL -- MAP_JON_RPC_WE_IF(..., !m_restricted) (src/rpc/core_rpc_server.h:166, :169,
# :170, :179) -- so the dispatch falls through to END_JSON_RPC_MAP(), which answers HTTP 200 with
#   {"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":<id>,"error":{"code":-32601,"message":"Method not found"}}
# (contrib/epee/include/net/http_server_handlers_map2.h:280-285). -32601 is the JSON-RPC 2.0
# "method not found" code; the message is epee's literal.
# A gated LEGACY endpoint behaves differently -- it leaves handled = false
# (http_server_handlers_map2.h:144) and epee answers HTTP 404
# (contrib/epee/include/net/http_protocol_handler.inl:664), with no body of this shape. fmonero-mock
# reproduces both halves: -32601 for a gated json_rpc method, 404 for a gated legacy endpoint.
# WHY IT MATTERS: `sync_info` answering -32601 IS fmonero's restricted-RPC probe
# (NodeClient::is_restricted, DESIGN.md §1b.2/§5b) -- the cheapest unambiguous one, and a call the
# node dashboard needs anyway. Under --restricted the mock answers this for sync_info,
# get_connections, get_bans and set_bans.
# `id` is a STRING here ("0"), matching DESIGN.md §8's literal. JSON-RPC 2.0 allows a string or a
# number and monerod echoes whatever it was sent, so a client must not assume either.
